title: PersonaGAN: Health-aware Conditional Stacked Adversarial Framework for Visualizing True Emotional States through Immersive Avatars
affiliations: Indian Institute of Information Technology Una, Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering,   CEG Campus, Anna University, Indian Institute of Information Technology Una and National Institute of Technology Agartala

detail.title: PersonaGAN: Health-aware Conditional Stacked Adversarial Framework for Visualizing True Emotional States through Immersive Avatars
detail.abstract: In recent years, wrist-worn devices have become integral to the continuous monitoring of physiological signals indicative of an individual’s internal affective and physical state. While prior studies have demonstrated the feasibility of detecting stress and emotional states from such data, but their outputs are typically limited to abstract indicators such as class labels, confidence scores, or statistical plots, which offer limited interpretability or experiential value to end users. In addition, many existing emotion recognition systems depend on externally observable cues, particularly facial expressions, which may not accurately reflect true emotional states when expressions are intentionally or unintentionally regulated. In contrast, emotional states derived from physiological signals provide a more reliable representation of true affect, but it remains underexplored in terms of intuitive and human-centered interactive visualization. This paper introduces PersonaGAN, a conditional stacked adversarial framework that translates wrist-worn physiological signals into expressive visual avatars designed for immersive augmented and virtual reality environments. Wrist-worn data from the WESAD dataset are preprocessed, normalized, and encoded into emotion-aware conditioning vectors that reflect internal affective responses without relying on facial cues. The proposed framework comprises a two-stage conditional stacked generative adversarial architecture with perceptual refinement, facilitating semantically coherent and visually realistic avatar generation. Next, the generated avatars are subsequently constructed into 3D representations using monocular depth estimation. Besides, a dedicated refinement pipeline is used to suppress background-induced artifacts, remove depth spikes, reconstruct missing surfaces via Poisson-based methods, and produce lightweight, 3D meshes suitable for Augment Reality and Virtual Reality (AR/VR) environments. Furthermore, the humanization pipeline integrates identity-preserving generation with expression transfer, enabling the creation of consistent and emotion-aware human avatars. The end-to-end pipeline is validated through Frechet Inception Distance (FID) based quantitative evaluation, qualitative visual assessment, and real-time deployment in AR and browser-based immersive VR environments using WebXR. Finally, experimental results indicate that our adversarial framework, achieves stable training with low FID scores, and works seamlessly in real time. Thus, proving geometry-aware, interpretable avatars that can effectively reflect a person’s internal emotions to support truly immersive human–computer experiences.

title: The Trade War Shocks and SOE's M&A as Local Bailouts:  Evidence from China
affiliations: Southwest University, Central University of Finance and Economics, Central University of Finance and Economics and Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE)

detail.title: The Trade War Shocks and SOE's M&A as Local Bailouts:  Evidence from China
detail.abstract: The trade war between U.S. and China is a vital and unexpected shock for Chinese firms, especially for private firms. This study examines the association between Chinese SOEs’ M&A decisions targeting private firms and trade-war shocks, offering a novel perspective on the Chinese government’s responses to trade-war shocks. Utilizing a comprehensive dataset of Chinese firms spanning from 2015 to 2021, we find that the trade war shocks dispute significantly increased the frequency of local acquisitions of private firms by SOEs. Cross-sectional analyses reveal that both managerial willingness to cooperate and local government pressure contribute to the heterogeneity of this behavior. Additional evidence shows that private firms directly exposed to the trade dispute are more likely to be acquired locally by SOEs. From the acquirers’ perspective, such local acquisitions yield short-term valuation gains but also lead to higher operating risk in the long run. From the regional perspective, these acquisitions help achieve the policy goal of “stabilizing employment,” yet they do not translate into significant improvements in local GDP rankings. Overall, our findings offer valuable insights regarding the broader economic implications of the trade war shocks and a collaborative perspective on state-owned and private enterprises during periods of economic uncertainty.

title: Gender Differences in STEM Faculty Productivity: An Empirical Analysis from India
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Houston and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Gender Differences in STEM Faculty Productivity: An Empirical Analysis from India
detail.abstract: Empirical literature on gender gaps in research productivity in STEM demonstrates that on average female scientists publish less and are cited less than their male counterparts within Global North contexts. We extend this literature to the Global South by using a one-of-a-kind multi-decade panel dataset comprising 1,45,666 distinct publications across 2,693 distinct faculty members belonging to the elite Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). Our choice of context is motivated by the notable career attrition of female scientists following STEM higher education in India. We conduct a career-trajectory analysis using fixed-effects modeling to study gender differences in number of publications, average impact factor and citations per paper over time. We demonstrate 3 key findings. While female faculty publish less than male faculty overall and at the start of their careers they begin to catch-up in the second decade of their career. On the other hand females publish in significantly better venues at the initial stage of their career but face a steeper decline than males in journal quality over time. Finally we find no statistically significant gender difference in the rate of citations per paper throughout the career cycle. Our findings provide evidence for the introduction of wide-ranging institutional policy targeted towards female faculty in STEM specifically during their early-career years. To our knowledge, our study is the first of its kind to analyze faculty productivity gaps within STEM in a developing country context, and therefore addresses a critical gap in the current literature on female retention and productivity in STEM careers globally.

title: Beyond the hype: Understanding IPO (over)valuation
affiliations: and Università della Svizzera italiana

detail.title: Beyond the hype: Understanding IPO (over)valuation
detail.abstract: IPOs frequently exhibit substantial price gains, which tend to diminish over time. We examine this phenomenon by focusing on the behavior of sophisticated and well-informed market participants, specifically short sellers and stock analysts. Our findings suggest that first-day closing prices often exceed fundamental values, driven by attention and sentiment-fueled buying pressure. Short sellers exploit these valuation distortions, likely at the expense of optimistic individual investors. Subsequently, analysts issue relatively conservative initial stock recommendations, contributing to a long-term decline in stock prices. Overall, waiting for post-IPO enthusiasm to subside may help investors avoid the overvaluation inherent in newly listed stocks.

title: From Identity to Consumption: The Role of Self-Brand Connection and Aspirational Motivation in Driving Symbolic and Status Consumption using M-D-O Framework
affiliations: Shandong University

detail.title: From Identity to Consumption: The Role of Self-Brand Connection and Aspirational Motivation in Driving Symbolic and Status Consumption using M-D-O Framework
detail.abstract: This study investigates how identity-related perceptions are transformed into consumption behavior within masstige retail environments by examining the psychological mechanisms linking consumers and brands. While prior research acknowledges the symbolic role of brands, limited attention has been given to the process through which identity alignment evolves into aspirational motivation and ultimately shapes consumption outcomes. Addressing this gap, the present research extends the Motivation–Desire–Outcome (M-D-O) framework by positioning self–brand connection as a relational mechanism that converts identity congruity into motivational energy driving marketplace behavior. Data were collected from consumers engaged with a leading masstige fashion retailer “Sapphire” and analyzed using PLS-SEM to evaluate a sequential mediation model. The findings indicate that identity alignment strengthens self–brand connection, which activates aspirational motivation and subsequently enhances both symbolic and status consumption tendencies. The results demonstrate that identity influences consumption primarily through indirect motivational pathways rather than direct effects alone. By integrating identity theory with consumer motivation perspectives, this study offers a process-based explanation of masstige consumption and highlights how retail brands operate as platforms enabling consumers to pursue desired self-concepts. The findings provide theoretical refinement and actionable insights for retailers seeking to cultivate meaningful consumer–brand relationships in emerging markets.

title: Analyzing Academic Mobility of NSF CAREER Award Winners
affiliations: University of Louisiana at Lafayette and Claremont Colleges - Claremont Graduate University

detail.title: Analyzing Academic Mobility of NSF CAREER Award Winners
detail.abstract: The study suggests that two highly regarded National Science Foundation (NSF) programs may, to some extent, be working at cross-purposes. The Established Program to Stimulate Competitive Research (EPSCoR) aims to strengthen the research infrastructure in states that traditionally have received less federal research support than the leading states. The NSF's Faculty Early Career Development Program (CAREER) program funds outstanding junior scholars throughout the nation to catalyze their research programs. We find that many CAREER award winners in EPSCoR states move to institutions in non-EPSCoR states. Frequently, they do so within the first five years after receiving this award. The study proposes a few targeted initiatives that institutions can implement.

title: Open Innovation, Absorptive Capacity, and Financial Health in Turbulent Technological Environments
affiliations: University of Southampton and Dalhousie University

detail.title: Open Innovation, Absorptive Capacity, and Financial Health in Turbulent Technological Environments
detail.abstract: As technological turbulence intensifies, evidence remains limited on how firms can translate open innovation into sustained financial returns. This study examines how open innovation intensity influences firms’ long-term financial health and develops an integrated framework linking external knowledge inputs, internal capabilities, and financial outcomes. Absorptive capacity is theorized as a key mediating mechanism, while technological turbulence is introduced as a moderating boundary condition. Using firm-level panel data and fixed-effects regression models, complemented by robustness and endogeneity tests, the analysis reveals three main findings. First, open innovation intensity has a significant and positive effect on long-term financial health, reflected in improved profitability quality, cash flow stability, and debt-servicing capacity. Second, absorptive capacity partially mediates this relationship, indicating that open innovation contributes to financial sustainability by strengthening firms’ ability to identify, assimilate, and exploit external knowledge. Third, technological turbulence amplifies this mechanism: under moderate to high levels of turbulence, the positive effect of open innovation on absorptive capacity is stronger. This study contributes theoretically by extending open innovation research from short-term innovation outcomes to long-term financial health and by clarifying the mediating role of absorptive capacity and the contingent role of technological turbulence. Practically, the findings suggest that firms should balance external collaboration with sustained internal investment in learning capabilities and strategically adjust openness in response to technological volatility to achieve durable financial resilience.

title: Analyzing the Impact of Credit Risk on BIST 100 Volatility Across Regimes
affiliations: Harvard University

detail.title: Analyzing the Impact of Credit Risk on BIST 100 Volatility Across Regimes
detail.abstract: This study analyzes the volatility structure of BIST 100 index returns by using the Markov Regime Switching VAR model. This is done within the framework of Turkish credit risk indicators. The attempted coup that occurred in July of 2016 has also been included in the model in order to investigate the impact that it has on volatility. Due to the data, it has been determined that the Asset Swap spread is superior to the other two credit risk indicators in terms of its ability to signal. The findings of the Markov Regime Switching experiment indicate that credit risk has little impact on the volatility of the BIST 100 return in regimes with low volatility. On the other hand, CDS, ASW, and ZV spreads have a considerable impact on volatility in regimes with high values of volatility. On the other hand, this impact can be disregarded due to the fact that its coefficient is very low. Last but not least, it is patently obvious that the attempted coup that took place in July 2016 and the activities that followed did not lead to an increase in the volatility of the BIST 100 returns.

title: Buyer Power and Corporate Innovation
affiliations: Nanjing University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Buyer Power and Corporate Innovation
detail.abstract: Moving beyond supply-side subsidies, this study investigates government procurement’s role in innovation using China’s National Centralized Volume-Based Procurement (VBP) policy. Employing a difference-in-differences approach, we find VBP significantly stimulates pharmaceutical R&D investment, fostering high-quality innovation more effectively than traditional instruments. The impact is strongest for winning bidders, non-state-owned enterprises, and firms heavily dependent on generic drugs. These findings underscore the government’s crucial role as a powerful buyer in driving innovation.

title: Industrial System Depth and the Geography of Technological Leadership
affiliations: Singapore University of Social Science

detail.title: Industrial System Depth and the Geography of Technological Leadership
detail.abstract: Why does full-spectrum technological autonomy---the capacity to independently sustain frontier technologies across the complete industrial stack---concentrate in a small set of countries, even as niche leadership has become more distributed? This paper develops three interconnected constructs. Industrial System Depth (ISD) measures the degree to which a national economy possesses vertically integrated productive capabilities spanning four hierarchically ordered layers: materials and components, capital equipment, manufacturing and assembly, and industrial software and services. Industrial System Gravity formalizes the mechanism by which deep industrial systems attract frontier technology industries through supply chain network effects, cross-layer knowledge spillovers, and fixed-cost amortization economies. The Scale Threshold Hypothesis proposes that each technological revolution raises the minimum effective scale required to sustain a complete industrial system, explaining why the club of technologically leading nations has not expanded despite centuries of knowledge diffusion. Using cross-national panel data for approximately 70 countries over 2000--2020, we construct an ISD index from manufacturing production, input-output linkage, and trade complexity data. Pooled OLS, country fixed effects, System GMM, and instrumental variable estimates consistently show that ISD and its interaction with national scale exhibit the strongest structural associations with frontier technology activity---beyond GDP, institutional quality, and export diversification. Threshold regressions identify a minimum scale below which industrial depth yields negligible innovation returns, and this threshold rises over the sample period. The framework contributes to innovation systems, economic complexity, and global value chain literatures by identifying industrial structure---not institutions alone---as a foundational determinant of technological leadership.

title: Optimizing the calibration of agent-based models throughreinforcement learning
affiliations: Catholic University of Milan, Bank of Italy, Università di Milano Cattolica and Catholic University of Milan

detail.title: Optimizing the calibration of agent-based models throughreinforcement learning
detail.abstract: The calibration of agent-based models (ABMs) in economics and finance typically involves searching for “satisfactory” parameter values over high-dimensional parameter spaces, a process that is both computationally intensive and highly sensitive to the choice of search algorithm. To address these challenges, we introduce a reinforcement learning (RL) method that adaptively selects and combines multiple search heuristics throughout the calibration process. We evaluate the proposed approach using the macroeconomic ABM developed by Assenza et al. (2015) (ADG) and demonstrate that it consistently outperforms both individual algorithms and conventional hybrid benchmarks. The method is further assessed on models from finance and epidemiology, highlighting its robustness and applicability across domains. Finally, we calibrate and validate the ADG model against empirical moments and examine its dynamic responses to structural shocks, comparing the resulting outcomes across alternative calibration strategies.

title: Container Loss at Sea as an Emerging Hazard to Coastal Fisheries: Evidence from Maritime Accident off Kerala, India
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN, and Center for Wireless Networks & Applications (WNA), Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham

detail.title: Container Loss at Sea as an Emerging Hazard to Coastal Fisheries: Evidence from Maritime Accident off Kerala, India
detail.abstract: Loss of maritime containers poses threats to coastal fisheries, particularly where major shipping routes intersect, yet their direct livelihood effects is poorly documented. This study demonstrates the fisheries impact of two recent maritime incidents off the Kerala coast, India, in May to June 2025: a sinking of MSC Elsa 3 and the explosion onboard MV Wan Hai 503. A rapid post-incident qualitative assessment (July – August 2025) was carried out using fishermen cooperative records and publicly available reports. Subsequent to the MSC Elsa 3 sinking, fishing cooperatives reported 26 gear-loss and boat damage cases on 21 fishing vessels, and totaling about 130,000 USD. Although 61 containers were found, more than 539 remained unrecovered, continuing to pose risks of gear loss in the location. Fishermen did not document any damage report after the Wan Hai 503 incident. These findings underscore the need for integrated maritime–fisheries governance, risk communication, rapid debris mapping, and robust compensation frameworks.

title: The Transparency Paradox: How Visual Clarity Amplifies Gender-Based Disparities in Digital Platforms
affiliations: Oklahoma City University

detail.title: The Transparency Paradox: How Visual Clarity Amplifies Gender-Based Disparities in Digital Platforms
detail.abstract: This study examines how host gender shapes economic outcomes in digital platforms through perceived trustworthiness (PTR) and how this relationship is conditioned by visual clarity. Using data from 2,709 Airbnb hosts with manually annotated visual features, we estimate a moderated mediation model linking gender, trust, and price. Results show a positive direct effect of male on price (β = 0.07, p < .01), but a negative indirect effect through PTR (β = −0.0126, 95% CI [−0.0222, −0.0035]), indicating competing pathways. Moreover, visual clarity significantly moderates this relationship. Under low clarity, the indirect effect is weak or non-significant (e.g., lighting: β = −0.0019, n.s.), whereas under high clarity it becomes stronger and significant (e.g., lighting: β = −0.0161, p < .01). Similar patterns emerge for image quality and color contrast. These findings show that improved visual clarity does not reduce bias but amplifies the effect of gender on trust and its downstream economic consequences, challenging assumptions that more diagnostic information leads to less biased evaluation.

title: ECONOMIA CIRCULAR EM COOPERATIVAS AGRÍCOLAS DA AMAZÔNIA SOCIOBIOECONOMIA
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: ECONOMIA CIRCULAR EM COOPERATIVAS AGRÍCOLAS DA AMAZÔNIA SOCIOBIOECONOMIA
detail.abstract: This study analyzes how barriers and synergies influence the adoption of circular economy practices in agricultural cooperatives of the Amazon sociobioeconomy, located in the northeastern region of Pará, Brazil. The research adopts a qualitative approach based on a multiple case study in two cooperatives. Data were collected through 42 semi-structured interviews with cooperative members, complemented by a literature review and document analysis. The data were examined using content analysis with deductive coding and abductive interpretation.The results indicate that circular economy practices are mainly concentrated in the reuse of organic waste, composting, and the use of bioinputs, representing incremental advances rather than structural transformation. Synergies were identified in environmental awareness, organizational practices, and institutional support from entities such as Sebrae and Senar. However, economic-financial, technical, political-legal, market, and climatic barriers operate interdependently, limiting the consolidation of circularity. Two emergent analytical codes were identified: collaboration ecosystem barriers and structural climatic barriers.The findings highlight the need to strengthen public policies, access to credit, and technical assistance to expand circular practices and promote sustainable territorial development. The study contributes by providing empirical evidence on circular economy adoption in Amazonian cooperatives, advancing the debate on circular transition in Global South contexts.

title: Behaviorally Grounded Agent-Based Benign Traffic Generation with LLM-Driven Action Variability for Intrusion Detection Evaluation
affiliations: University of Malaga, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Behaviorally Grounded Agent-Based Benign Traffic Generation with LLM-Driven Action Variability for Intrusion Detection Evaluation
detail.abstract: Machine-learning-based intrusion and anomaly-detection systems require benign training data that is both diverse and representative of operational networks. In practice, however, collecting and sharing real network traces is constrained by privacy, confidentiality, and organizational policies, while many synthetic datasets lack behavioral realism and offer limited transparency regarding how the traffic was generated. We present a behaviorally grounded framework for benign traffic generation in which autonomous agents emulate distinct user roles and produce traffic through real application execution rather than packet-, flow-, or feature-level synthesis. For the regular-user profile, action instantiation is guided by a constrained large language model planner that samples profile-consistent intents and query terms under a fixed output schema. This introduces controlled non-determinism at the action layer while preserving the realism of actual application use. The framework comprises traffic-generating agents, an isolated execution and capture environment, and a packet-level analysis pipeline. Three representative profiles are instantiated: a regular user engaged in web-centric activity, a gamer combining latency-sensitive application traffic with real-time communication, and a network administrator dominated by encrypted remote-management actions. Traffic is captured as PCAP traces using standard tools and analyzed in terms of protocol composition, flow structure, temporal dynamics, and variability. Results show distinct, profile-consistent transport mixes, service and port footprints, and throughput dynamics across repeated sessions, supporting the use of the generated traces as controlled benign baselines for IDS/NDR experimentation. The methodology emphasizes protocol semantics and session structure, complements statistical and feature-space generators, and remains procedurally reproducible without relying on real user traces.

title: A Precise and Efficient Method for Converting Complex Natural Language Queries into Standard SQL Statements
affiliations: Wuxi University, Wuxi University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Wuxi University, Wuxi University, Wuxi University and Wuxi University

detail.title: A Precise and Efficient Method for Converting Complex Natural Language Queries into Standard SQL Statements
detail.abstract: Complex natural language to SQL (CNL2SQL) aims to map natural-language queries involving nested reasoning structures, such as subqueries, aggregation, grouped filtering, and multi-table joins, to their corresponding SQL statements. However, directly applying large language models (LLMs) to CNL2SQL often yields unsatisfactory performance, particularly for structurally complex queries. To address this issue, we propose a precise SQL generation method tailored to complex queries. Experimental results show that the proposed approach is robust and adaptable across multiple business database scenarios and consistently improves generation accuracy for complex queries. On a dataset of 600 real-world queries spanning the education, enterprise management, e-commerce, and video-rental domains, the proposed method achieves a conversion accuracy of 91.2%, outperforming existing methods and direct LLM-based conversion.

title: Internal ESG Perceptions and Firm-Level Sustainability Outcomes: Evidence on Innovation and Competitive Dynamics in Vietnam
affiliations: Jiangsu University and Jiangsu University

detail.title: Internal ESG Perceptions and Firm-Level Sustainability Outcomes: Evidence on Innovation and Competitive Dynamics in Vietnam
detail.abstract: This research examines the impact of workers' views of ESG practices on corporate sustainability. Specifically, it explores how employee attitudes toward ESG influence green innovation, competitive dynamics, and firm performance—mechanisms through which internal perspectives shape outcomes. This inquiry is especially pertinent in developing nations, where such dynamics are less understood. Clarifying these mechanisms is essential for successful ESG initiatives. Data were gathered from 373 companies across various industries in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was used to examine the links between employee ESG attitudes, green innovation, competitive advantage, and corporate sustainability performance. The study combines stakeholder theory with the resource-based approach to provide a mechanism-based explanation of the findings. The results indicate that favourable employee opinions of ESG policies significantly improve green innovation and bolster competitive advantage. These elements, thus, have a significant beneficial impact on corporate sustainability results. The report emphasizes workers' perspectives as a vital internal mechanism linking ESG activities to capability development, innovation, and sustained competitiveness Managers and policymakers in developing economies must emphasise internal ESG involvement, ensuring that staff are informed about and aligned with sustainability goals. By cultivating favourable opinions, companies may stimulate innovation, augment competitiveness, and elevate sustainability performance. Incorporating ESG principles into the structure is crucial for sustained economic and environmental advantages. Employee views of ESG are crucial determinants of green innovation, advantage in the marketplace, and sustainable organizational performance.

title: Who Can Admit Luck? CEO Success Narratives, Legitimacy, and Diversity in Executive Leadership
affiliations: Universidad EAFIT and Tecnologico de Monterrey

detail.title: Who Can Admit Luck? CEO Success Narratives, Legitimacy, and Diversity in Executive Leadership
detail.abstract: Executive leaders are routinely asked to narrate "how they made it", and these success narratives play a central role in how organisations learn about leadership and diversity. Yet not all CEOs can tell the same kinds of stories. Building on a qualitative analysis of eleven book-length biographies of prominent CEOs sampled across race, gender, and class origin, this study examines how structural position shapes whether executives can publicly attribute success to luck or to merit.We identify a systematic pattern. Highly privileged CEOs (white, male, upper-class leaders) freely acknowledge luck, structural advantages, and informal help in their trajectories, and such acknowledgements enhance perceptions of humility and wisdom. By contrast, CEOs from marginalised backgrounds (women and racialised leaders from working-class origins) emphatically deny luck and over-perform meritocratic narratives to defend their legitimacy against suspected tokenism.We theorise narrative legitimacy constraints and legitimacy traps as mechanisms linking structural privilege to unequal narrative freedom in leadership attribution. These mechanisms generate a diversity learning paradox: the leaders whose experiences could most inform inclusive leadership and effective DEI practices are the least able to speak openly about structural conditions that enabled their success, whereas privileged leaders can reflect candidly on luck without jeopardising their standing.We discuss implications for theories of executive and responsible leadership, leadership attribution, and the design of leadership development and diversity initiatives that rely on CEO storytelling as a tool for organisational learning.

title: UAV-based search and rescue routing problem with environmental risk assessment
affiliations: Southwest Jiaotong University, Southwest Jiaotong University and Chongqing University

detail.title: UAV-based search and rescue routing problem with environmental risk assessment
detail.abstract: This paper studies a novel Heterogeneous UAV Team Orienteering Problem for flood disaster search and rescue, integrating environmental risk assessment and precedence constraints. Each affected location may require a sequence of two specialized tasks, namely initial thermal screening followed by visual confirmation, which must be performed in a strict order by a heterogeneous fleet of drones. The rescue profit for each location is defined as a time-decaying function of its comprehensive risk index. We formulate the problem as a mixed-integer programming model and design a tailored Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) heuristic to solve this NP-hard problem. A real-world case study in Guangxi, China, and extensive computational experiments demonstrate that this environment-driven approach effectively optimizes drone allocation to maximize lifesaving efficacy. Computational experiments demonstrated the efficiency of the ALNS in obtaining high-quality solutions for large-scale cases. This study provides a decision-support framework that bridging environmental risk analysis with routing optimization.

title: Collaborative Optimization of Corn Supply Chain Loss Reduction under Carbon Emission Constraints
affiliations: Dalian Maritime University, Dalian Maritime University, Dalian Maritime University and Heilongjiang Bayi Agricultural University

detail.title: Collaborative Optimization of Corn Supply Chain Loss Reduction under Carbon Emission Constraints
detail.abstract: This study focuses on the loss-reduction problem of corn supply chain under the constraints of carbon emissions. A sequential decision mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model is constructed with the objective of minimizing the total cost of processing enterprises, integrating the seasonal variability of raw grain supply, inventory losses, as well as timeliness, costs, losses, and carbon footprint of different transportation modes and its packaging types in both direct and transshipment operations. With customized dynamic programming embedded in branch-and-price algorithm, a series of case studies are conducted in critical scenarios of China’s ”North-to-South grain transportation”. It is found that cumulative carbon constraints result in lower costs compared to full-cycle, periodic, or fluctuating carbon-constraint strategies. For the adoption of bulk-to-container transport, the cost-sharing threshold of return shipments is 125.417 CNY/TEU under transshipment conditions and 340.455 CNY/TEU under direct-shipment conditions. These results provide incredible insights for addressing coordination bottlenecks in grain supply chains.

title: Understanding hourly production workers’ technology acceptance behaviour of Generative AI in manufacturing
affiliations: Mississippi State University, Mississippi State University, The Pennsylvania State University (University Park) – Penn State Law, Mississippi State University, Oklahoma State University and MedStar Georgetown University Hospital

detail.title: Understanding hourly production workers’ technology acceptance behaviour of Generative AI in manufacturing
detail.abstract: Manufacturers are investing in generative AI (genAI), yet technology-acceptance theory rarely examines hourly production workers. We extend the Technology Acceptance Model by incorporating Five Factor Model traits, General Attitudes toward AI Scale, and Computer Self-Efficacy. Survey data from hourly workers at four manufacturing sites, collected after exposure to a genAI use case, test predictors of perceived usefulness and ease of use. Regression results show attitudes toward AI and computer self-efficacy consistently predict both outcomes, while personality traits add limited explanatory power. Shop-floor acceptance appears driven more by sociotechnical perceptions and perceived competence than stable dispositions.

title: Tradable Credit Schemes for Decarbonization: Insights from a Real-Life Trial at a University
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, VU University Amsterdam and Technische Universität München (TUM)

detail.title: Tradable Credit Schemes for Decarbonization: Insights from a Real-Life Trial at a University
detail.abstract: Tradable Credit Schemes (TCS) are a promising policy instrument for reducing transportation externalities. Their political feasibility may be higher than that of taxes, since policymakers can steer distributional outcomes through the initial allocation of credits, which may in turn increase acceptability. However, TCS require complex decision-making by participants, making empirical evidence on user behavior essential. We conducted a multi-week randomized controlled trial with over 600 participants in a university setting to evaluate the effects of a TCS on commuting emissions. Specifically, we implemented the MobilityCoin system, which prices CO2 emissions. While 18% of the treatment group reported changes in their commuting behavior, compared to 10% in the control group, econometric analysis shows only weak evidence of emission reductions in the full sample. Significant effects are found for specific subgroups, such as public transport users. We find no evidence that participants respond to variation in the price level. Our distance-based allocation leads to progressive outcomes: low-income participants benefit financially on average and do not appear to bear a disproportionate behavioral burden. In terms of acceptability, a majority of treated participants evaluate the system favorably, with more than one-third supporting its implementation at the university. Overall, our results highlight the potential of TCS as a policy instrument: they can induce behavioral change in specific populations while achieving progressive distributional outcomes and relatively high public acceptance.

title: From Governance Design To Governance Enactment: How Managerial Cognition And Emotion Shape Alliance Legitimacy Under Institutional Plurality
affiliations: Ramapo College of New Jersey

detail.title: From Governance Design To Governance Enactment: How Managerial Cognition And Emotion Shape Alliance Legitimacy Under Institutional Plurality
detail.abstract: Cross-border alliances frequently unravel despite being contractually robust and strategically aligned. Prior international business research has predominantly explained these failures through contractual incompleteness, institutional weakness, or environmental volatility. This article advances an alternative explanation by foregrounding governance enactment—the micro-level processes through which managers interpret, emotionally appraise, and act upon formal governance arrangements under conditions of institutional plurality.Adopting a microfoundational perspective, the study develops a conceptual model integrating managerial cognition, cultural intelligence, and emotion-driven sensemaking to explain how formal governance is translated into practice. These intertwined processes determine whether alliances build relational legitimacy and stability or instead spiral into conflict and disengagement.The argument is grounded in three illustrative cases from African business contexts, treated not as anomalies but as theory-revealing environments in which institutional plurality renders microfoundational mechanisms unusually visible. The cases show that formally similar governance structures yield divergent outcomes depending on how managers construe obligations, negotiate legitimacy, and respond to stakeholder claims. They reveal how emotional appraisal interacts with sensemaking to shape governance enactment.The study contributes to international management research by: (1) reframing alliance failure as a governance enactment problem rather than a structural deficiency; (2) establishing emotional appraisal as a theoretically distinct and constitutive mechanism; (3) reconceptualizing legitimacy as an emergent, processual outcome of enacted governance under institutional plurality; and (4) demonstrating how African contexts generate generalizable theory.

title: A Rising Tide that Lifts All Boats: The Effects of Collective Recognition Programs on E-Commerce Sellers
affiliations: , Zhejiang University, University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Anderson School of Management and Zhejiang University

detail.title: A Rising Tide that Lifts All Boats: The Effects of Collective Recognition Programs on E-Commerce Sellers
detail.abstract: Platform certifications typically recognize individual sellers or products, yet the effects of collective, community-level certification remain unexplored. Alibaba’s Taobao Town Certification (TTC) exemplifies this by recognizing all sellers in a rural town “collectively” once their combined e-commerce activity reaches a set milestone. By applying signaling and social identity theories, we develop a theoretical framework with two channels: (1) a demand-side channel, where the collective certification signals “commercial viability” to buyers, reducing the perceived risk of purchasing from rural sellers in these certified towns; and (2) a supply-side channel, where TTC elevates the salience of the town’s “collective identity,” motivating sellers to specialize and align with the town’s core strengths. Using quarterly seller panel data from four Chinese provinces and a causal forest difference-in-differences design, we show that sellers in these TTC-certified towns saw a 13.8% increase in quarterly sales and an 8.8% increase in the number of orders. Moreover, the TTC program does not lead to “diversification” in these TTC-certified towns; instead, individual sellers concentrate on the town’s signature products. The second-stage heterogeneity analysis further reveals that the effect is stronger for sellers in less-developed areas and regions with high collectivism. Our findings offer platform managers and policymakers actionable insights for designing collective certification programs that promote regional economic development through shared recognition.
